answer: Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. Each submission hangs on the island of a task receipt, and the inlet is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. The marble of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. The design leans on reciprocity-weighted attestation, reset on any identity-link attempt, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool. Written in a cause and effect, two sentences register, it stays short.
